ai.literal: Nature having-known, [in] strong assembly mouth they-slip-not, of-word collection who-knew purity they.
ai.translation: Those pure ones who have mastered a multitude of words will not falter in their speech before a formidable assembly, having understood its nature.
ai.modern: சொற்களின் தொகுதியை அறிந்த தூய்மையானவர்கள், அவையின் தன்மையை நன்கு அறிந்து, வல்லவர்கள் நிறைந்த அவையில் பேசும்போது வாய் தவறிப் பேச மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the confidence of well-prepared speakers in a learned assembly. 'சொல்லின் தொகை' (the collection of words) refers to a deep mastery of vocabulary and rhetoric, while 'தூய்மை' (purity) points to their clarity of mind and flawless speech. By understanding the nature ('வகை') of the powerful council ('வல் அவை'), these pure and knowledgeable individuals will never let a wrong word slip from their mouths ('வாய் சோரார்'). The verse emphasizes that true mastery of language prevents faltering even before the most intimidating audiences.

ai.literal: Among the learned, learned they will be called: before the learned, things learned so as to reach, those who speak.
ai.translation: Those who can speak what they have learned so that it reaches the minds of the learned are called the most learned among the learned.
ai.modern: கற்ற அறிஞர்களின் முன்னே, தாம் கற்றவற்றை அவர்கள் மனத்தில் பதியும்படி தெளிவாகச் சொல்ல வல்லவர்களே, கற்றவர்களுள் சிறந்த கற்றவர்கள் என்று சிறப்பித்துச் சொல்லப்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the highest tier of scholarship as the ability to communicate effectively. The phrase 'kaṟṟāruḷ kaṟṟār' means 'the learned among the learned', indicating exceptional scholars. To earn this title, one must not merely possess knowledge, but be able to speak ('colluvār') what they have learned ('kaṟṟa') before an assembly of experts ('kaṟṟār muṉ'). The crucial word here is 'cela', which literally means 'to go' or 'to reach', signifying that the speaker's words must successfully penetrate the minds of the audience and be accepted by them.

ai.literal: Enemy inside those who die are easy; rare are assembly inside those who fear not.
ai.translation: Those who bravely die on the battlefield are easy to find. Rare are those who stand without fear in an assembly.
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தில் பகைவர்களுக்கு அஞ்சாமல் சாகத் துணிபவர்கள் உலகில் பலர் உள்ளனர். ஆனால் கற்றவர் நிறைந்த சபையில் பேச அஞ்சாதவர்கள் மிகவும் சிலரே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts physical courage with intellectual courage. It states that finding warriors willing to die on the battlefield is relatively easy. However, finding individuals who can stand before a learned assembly and speak without fear is truly rare. The repetition of the word 'agattu' (inside) draws a direct parallel between the battlefield and the assembly hall, highlighting that facing an audience requires a rarer kind of bravery.

ai.literal: Learned ones before, learned things to reach having spoken, oneself learned things, those who are greater among, greater things taking.
ai.translation: Speak what you have learned convincingly before the learned; and from those who are more learned, grasp what is greater than your own learning.
ai.modern: கற்றறிந்த அறிஞர்கள் முன்னே தான் கற்றவற்றை அவர்கள் மனத்தில் பதியுமாறு தெளிவாகச் சொல்ல வேண்டும். அதே சமயம், தன்னை விட அதிகமாகக் கற்ற அறிஞர்களிடமிருந்து தான் கற்றதை விட மேலான கருத்துகளைக் கேட்டு அறிந்துகொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the dual responsibility of a learned person in an assembly. First, one must articulate their own knowledge clearly and convincingly before other scholars. Second, one must remain humble and receptive, actively acquiring deeper knowledge from those who are more learned. The word 'செல' (to go/reach) emphasizes that speaking is not just uttering words, but ensuring the ideas successfully reach and convince the audience's minds.

ai.literal: Properly, the measure having known, let one learn, assembly not-fearing reply giving for the sake of.
ai.translation: Let one learn the proper measure of subjects thoroughly, in order to give fearless replies in the assembly.
ai.modern: அவையில் பயப்படாமல் தகுந்த பதிலைச் சொல்வதற்காக, நூல்களின் அளவை முறையாக அறிந்து கற்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of thorough and proper learning for effective public speaking. The phrase 'ஆற்றின் அளவு அறிந்து' means knowing the proper extent and method of subjects. One must learn deeply so that they can confidently give an 'அஞ்சா மாற்றம்' (fearless reply) when questioned in an assembly. True confidence in a council comes from the depth and clarity of one's knowledge.

ai.literal: With a sword, what, to those who are not brave? With a book, what, to those who fear a subtle assembly?
ai.translation: What use is a sword to those who lack courage? What use is learning to those who fear an assembly of subtle minds?
ai.modern: வீரம் இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு வாளால் என்ன பயன்? அதுபோலவே, கூர்மையான அறிவுடையோர் நிறைந்த அவையைக் கண்டு அஞ்சுபவர்களுக்கு அவர்கள் கற்ற நூல்களால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a striking analogy to emphasize the importance of confidence in public speaking. It compares a coward holding a sword to a timid scholar facing an assembly. Just as a weapon is useless to someone without bravery (வன்கண்), extensive learning (நூல்) is of no value to someone who is afraid to speak before an assembly of sharp, subtle thinkers (நுண் அவை). The repeated question 'என்' (what use) highlights that tools and knowledge require inner strength to be effective.

ai.literal: enemy inside timid-person hand bright-sword assembly inside fearing he learned text
ai.translation: The learning of a man who is afraid to speak in an assembly is like a sharp sword in the hands of a coward on the battlefield.
ai.modern: அவையில் பேசப் பயப்படுகிறவன் கற்ற நூலானது, போர்க்களத்தில் பகைவர் நடுவே ஒரு பேடியின் கையில் இருக்கும் கூர்மையான வாளைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid simile to illustrate the uselessness of knowledge if one lacks the courage to share it. It compares a learned person who is terrified of speaking in an assembly to a timid person holding a bright, sharp sword on a battlefield. Just as the sword is of no use to someone too frightened to fight, the texts learned by a scholar are worthless if he is too afraid to present his knowledge before a council. The word 'பேடி' (timid person or coward) emphasizes the complete lack of necessary courage in a critical situation.

ai.literal: many - those things - even having learned - benefit - they are without indeed - good - assembly-in - well - to reach - those who do not speak
ai.translation: Those who cannot speak well and convincingly in a good assembly derive no benefit at all, even if they have learned many things.
ai.modern: நல்ல அறிஞர்கள் நிறைந்த அவையில், அவர்கள் மனம் ஏற்குமாறு நன்றாகப் பேச முடியாதவர்கள், பல நூல்களைக் கற்றிருந்தாலும் அதனால் ஒரு பயனும் இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that mere accumulation of knowledge is useless if one cannot communicate it effectively. The word 'அவை' appears twice with different meanings: first as 'those things' (referring to subjects of study) and then as 'assembly'. The phrase 'நன்கு செல' (to go well) vividly captures the idea of words reaching and penetrating the minds of the audience. Even if a person has learned many subjects, their learning yields no benefit ('பயமிலரே') if they lack the courage and skill to articulate it clearly in a gathering of good scholars.

ai.literal: Than the unlearned, the lowest, they say, having learned and even having known, the good people's assembly those who fear.
ai.translation: They say that those who have learned and understood much, yet fear the assembly of the good, are lower than the unlearned.
ai.modern: நூல்களைக் கற்றும் அவற்றின் பொருளை அறிந்தும், நல்லவர்களின் அவைக்குப் பேச அஞ்சுபவர்கள், படிக்காதவர்களை விடக் கீழானவர்கள் என்று அறிஞர்கள் கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of knowledge without the courage to share it. The phrase 'கற்று அறிந்தும்' shows that the person has both acquired and deeply understood their learning. Yet, if they fear ('அஞ்சுவார்') speaking in the assembly of good and wise people ('நல்லார் அவை'), their education serves no purpose. Consequently, they are judged to be even lower ('கடை') than those who have never learned at all ('கல்லாதவரின்').

ai.literal: They exist, even if, with those who do not exist they are equal, assembly having feared, things learned to go those who do not speak.
ai.translation: Those who fear the assembly and fail to speak their learning convincingly are equal to the dead, even though they are alive.
ai.modern: அவைக்குப் பயந்து தாங்கள் கற்றவற்றைப் பிறர் ஏற்குமாறு சொல்லத் தெரியாதவர்கள், உயிரோடு இருந்தாலும் இறந்தவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பானவர்களே.
ai.explanation: This couplet strongly condemns the inability to share one's knowledge in public due to stage fright. The phrase 'களன் அஞ்சி' means fearing the assembly of scholars, while 'செலச் சொல்லாதார்' refers to those who cannot communicate their learning so that it reaches and convinces the listeners. Because their knowledge remains unshared and useless to the world, the poet declares that even if they are physically alive ('உளர் எனினும்'), they are no different from the dead ('இல்லாரொடு ஒப்பர்').
